text:
Alex: FYI hitting a customer issue — their outbound firewall only allows specific IP ranges + ports to our egress. We saw 502s when they switched to transparent proxy mode.
Priya: Do we have a truly stable set of egress IPs per region or do ranges rotate with scale events? Customer needs CIDRs for their rule-of-law.
Alex: For hosted we publish region CIDRs but they can expand/contract. For Dedicated we allocate from per-tenant NAT pools; source IP can vary by node. Their security team insists on static source IPs.
Jamal: We can offer tenant-assigned static EIP/NATs, but note the tradeoffs: cost, limited pool size, and SNAT port exhaustion risk under high concurrent connections.
Lin: Another gotcha — customer uses split-tunnel VPN + split-horizon DNS. Their internal DNS resolves our FQDN to private addresses and routes some traffic via corporate proxy and some direct. That breaks SNI-based routing and header-based allowlists.
Priya: They also require all outbound to go through their HTTP proxy (CONNECT only) with TLS inspection. So they will only allow destination IPs for the proxy host and 443 to our endpoints. Does our LB hostname have to be allowlisted or just the IPs?
Alex: If they use an explicit proxy they should allow the proxy host IPs and proxy port. If they rely on transparent routing, they need our egress CIDRs. Recommend customers allow hostnames for proxies + a CIDR fallback.
Jamal: Practical guidance to publish: (a) per-region stable CIDR blocks for firewall rules, (b) dedicated static-EIP option for tenants who need fixed IPs, (c) recommended minimum number of IPs per concurrency (see calc below).
Lin: SNAT math quick note: per IPv4 we have ~64k ephemeral ports. Reserve for OS and ephemeral reuse — assume 50k usable ports. That means ~50k concurrent connections per IP before exhaustion; for long-lived streams assume much lower. Recommend 2 IPs per 10k long-lived connections.
Alex: Also add a small healthcheck endpoint customers can curl to verify mapping: code block:
```
curl -s https://egress-health.redwood-inference.prod/your-tenant/which-ip
# returns {"observed_ip": "34.72.129.45", "region": "us-west-2", "asn": "AS15169"}
```
Priya: We should document proxy-chaining behavior: if customer terminates TLS and re-establishes upstream (TLS inspect), Host header and SNI may differ. Tell customers to allow either the LB hostname or the per-region CIDR if TLS inspect is in place.
Jamal: Also call out hairpin/hairpinning tests — NAT hairpinning breaks when customers use the same external IP for internal services. Provide this test command for customers behind a proxy/NAT: `curl -vk --resolve mysvc.redwood:443:34.72.129.45 https://mysvc.redwood/` to validate SNI+cname mapping.
deploy-bot: deploy completed on prod-egress-us-west-2 at 2026-03-18T12:04:22Z :rocket:
Priya: Action items: update docs with per-region stable CIDRs + static EIP option, publish SNAT sizing guidance, add the healthcheck endpoint and example curl commands. Also include a short checklist for proxy mode vs transparent mode.
Alex: I'll create the RFC/ticket and loop in infra-eng and support. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Lin: I'll DM infra-eng to reserve 4 extra EIPs for the pilot tenant and run a port-usage simulation this week.
Priya: Also remind the customer to allow outbound DNS (UDP/53) or TCP/53 to their resolvers; split-horizon DNS will otherwise resolve to internal addresses and break routing.
